title: sail commands read an atlas as one input
body:
`sail` subcommands take data files and stdin as inputs. An atlas written by `sail atlas` (sail-2413e6) cannot be passed to any of them.

## Proposal

Every subcommand accepts an atlas wherever it accepts a data file, and reads it as one input whose records are numbered as one run across its parts. `sail get all.satlas 500` counts across files, and `sail skim all.satlas -n 1000` draws from all of them. That differs from `sail get a.fa b.fa 500`, where each file is its own input with its own numbering.

- An input is an atlas when it opens with the magic `SLAT`, read the way `format::detect` reads a data file's first bytes. The extension plays no part.
- The stream backend reads it through `Readers` with the atlas's counts, so `sail skim` needs no counting pass. The indexed backend reads it through `Aggregate`. The memory backend loads every part.
- An atlas with a stale part is refused. The error names the part and says to run `sail atlas` again (sail-978552).

Built on sail-3a486e, which adds the `libsail` constructors.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/424f83e5
notes.text: When this lands, drop 'No command reads an atlas yet.' from the `atlas` entry in `sail/CHANGELOG.md`, and describe reading an atlas in the README's 'reading large files' section.
